channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: France Officials Acknowledge ‘Failure’ Around Riots
item.description: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu defended police efforts and pledged to restore order as government ministers acknowledged failures.

item.title: NPR: Australian prime minister says lawmaker critically injured by car is 'no accident'
item.description: A car hit an Australian federal independent lawmaker on Monday, critically injuring her in an apparent deliberate attack, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. The driver was arrested.

item.title: BBC News: Watch: Are the French riots a warning of an intense election to come?
item.description: Rioting, looting and vandalism has gripped France over the weekend after protests spiralled out of control across the country.

item.title: The Guardian: Can countries deliver on a deal to save the world’s plants and animals?
item.description: Four years ago nearly every government on Earth agreed to protect nature. Now, as countries gather for Cop17, the pressure is on to follow through on those commitments Cop17 at a glance: everything you need to know about…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Iran War backlash threatens Republican control of Congress
item.description: Public opposition to the Iran War could threaten Republican control of Congress, as economic fallout fuels voter anger.

item.title: Ars Technica: Huge DMV data breach impacted current and former Florida residents
item.description: Florida issues alerts after statewide DMV data breach linked to ShinyHunters.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Nathan Fielder’s Surprise Call From Elizabeth Holmes: ‘I Trust You’
item.description: The codirector of “You Can See Everything” talks exclusively to WIRED about truth, lies, and Theranos.

item.title: WIRED Science: How Elizabeth Holmes Tricked WIRED—and Everyone Else
item.description: WIRED was the first magazine to cover Theranos and its enticing billionaire founder. There were warning signs even then.

item.title: WIRED Business: The Story of Billy Evans and ‘Theranos 2.0’
item.description: Elizabeth Holmes’ husband is a major figure in Nathan Fielder’s new documentary. But who is Billy Evans—and is he really working on a second blood-testing company?

item.title: The New Yorker: The New Age of Reading
item.description: Alarm about declining interest in books is perpetual. But, as bookselling reaches unexpected heights, James Daunt, the chief executive of Barnes & Noble, thinks a different future is at hand.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: The Beauty Products Celebrity Aesthetician Andrea Ámez Uses to the Last Drop
item.description: She adores Cetaphil cleanser, Osmosis serum, and Santa Maria Novella bodywash.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: A Greenwood Heights Duplex With a Backyard and Skylight for $950,000
item.description: And a one-bedroom with triple exposures and church views on lower Fifth Avenue.

item.title: Fox59: Chris Ballard out as Colts general manager
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS – The tenure of Colts general manager Chris Ballard reached its end. He was fired Monday morning by principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon. The status of Ballard had been in serious question as the Colts’ playo…

item.title: Mirror Indy: “There’s room for everyone in the clown car”
item.description: Indy’s drag performers see clowning as a way to find acceptance and reclaim their childhood. The post “There’s room for everyone in the clown car” appeared first on Mirror Indy .
